newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel says talk of easing EMU rules baseless.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel says talk of easing EMU rules baseless.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Monday that rumours that the rules for taking part in European monetary union would be eased were without foundation.
"There will be no divergence from the stability criteria," Kinkel said in a statement. "Rumours of such considerations are totally baseless."

Kinkel was speaking after Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition voted key parts of a major austerity package into law last week, bidding to ensure Germany meets borrowing targets in 1997 set by the Maastricht treaty to qualify for EMU in 1999.
"The coalition continues to hold firm that currency union will come on the agreed date of January 1, 1999. Waverers, hesitators and delayers must not have a chance," Kinkel said.
He was speaking following newspaper speculation last week that France and Germany had struck a secret deal to ease the terms of monetary union.

Both countries are working on deficit-slashing austerity measures to bring their budget shortfalls within the Maastricht limit of three percent of gross domestic product in 1997 -- the year fitness to join EMU will be judged.
